b1-unit-61.61.1 Danny's blog: eight habits I picked:
Danny: Eight habits I picked up in Brazil. When I arrived in São Paulo, my habits were a disaster. Here are eight good ones I've picked up from the people around me.
Danny: Thanks to my seven a.m. classes, I'm now an early riser. Ana calls me at one minute past six, and she'll always ask the same question: "Are you out of bed?" Getting up early gives me an extra hour that I never used to have.
Danny: Back home, I'd buy things I didn't need just because they were on sale. Here, I'm saving for a trip to the Amazon, so I write down everything I spend. It's boring, but it works.
Danny: Mrs. Lima will put rice, beans and a salad on the table every day, and she won't accept "I'm not hungry" as an answer. I've stopped snacking on junk food at night. Well, almost.
Danny: Bruno is always telling me to get out of the city. On our trip to the Pantanal, I spent a week without a screen, and I didn't miss it at all.
Danny: Bruno runs every morning with Pipoca, and he kept inviting me until I said yes. Now I go twice a week. Pipoca is still faster than both of us.
Danny: Grandma Lourdes is ninety-seven, and she still does a crossword every morning to learn new words. When I complain about Portuguese verbs, I think of her and study for fifteen more minutes.
Danny: Rafa has a rule: one evening a week is just for music, and nothing can change it. I've copied him. On Thursday evenings, I switch off my phone and read.
Danny: My grandfather would always say, "Stop worrying about tomorrow and enjoy your coffee." I didn't understand him then. I do now. My worst habit? I keep checking my phone during dinner. Mrs. Lima is always complaining about it, and she's right.
